Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and then use the wake-visual-signals skill to inspect the current rollout keyframes before touching the target policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t use the omitted research shelf.

The skill’s required evidence pass is now active: I’m anchoring the images to the sampled scores, observations, metrics, and inherited guidance first. I’ll compare the shared prewarm state and rollout sheets before writing the diagnosis or editing the candidate.

The evidence is unusually clean: all four sampled solver rollouts are byte-identical gain-1.7 candidates and trajectories, each capturing at 39.710. The inherited gain-1.725 test is the key negative comparator—it still captures but is slower and has higher crossflow and loads—so another tiny gain interpolation is not supported. I’m now tracing the existing policy/state contract to choose one bounded, separately testable axis.

The wake-visual skill now requires the pre-edit record, so I’m writing the diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis before changing the policy. The candidate will keep the replicated gain-1.7 gait and total steering command, and test only the steering distribution: shifting the anterior fraction from 0.40 to 0.45 to reduce the observed posterior joint excursion imbalance without introducing an unscaled signal.

The single candidate and both required provenance files are now updated. The reusable lesson records the replicated gain-1.7 anchor, the failed 1.725 interpolation, and the bounded allocation axis with its wake-phase boundary; I’m moving to the prescribed non-CFD checks now.

The prescribed guidance check found a rendered-workspace defect before evaluating my lesson: `README.md` contains the same assigned-parent marker twice, while the checker requires exactly one. I’m inspecting the checker and will remove only the duplicate marker if that is the sole cause, then rerun it.

The guidance check now passes. The exact Julia contract command cannot start because no `julia` executable is installed on this runner (exit 127); I’ll still run the independent boundary and deterministic parameter-schema checks, without launching CFD.

I’ve executed the three prescribed checks directly; to satisfy the workspace’s explicit “invoke check-runner” requirement, I’m also handing the final verification to the configured check-runner role. It will run only the listed non-CFD checks and report the environment-limited Julia result.
